newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend cautious advance on GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend cautious advance on GDP data.

text.p: Mexican stocks began to shake off their early apathy and increase gains in early afternoon trade on Monday in the wake of favorable GDP data, dealers said.
"The market is listless. The GDP figures were good and woke us up a bit, but dealers will wait until tomorrow's FOMC meeting before really stepping in," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 12.93 points, or 0.33 percent, at 3,903.29.

Mexico's Finance Ministry announced shortly after mid-session that first quarter GDP in 1997 had increased by 5.1 percent in real terms when compared with the same period last year. A Reuters survey MEX22 of financial firms conducted prior to the data predicted an average increase of 5.12 percent.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday to review U.S. interest rate policy.
"It is a little above consensus, which will calm things down today," a desk trader said.
Dealers said foreign investors were tentatively entering the market.
"They're very selective and not very active, but they are buying low," a trader said.
Cross trades accounted for more than half of a total 58.8 million shares traded.
Of 96 stocks traded, 38 were ahead while 31 had declined.
